description: Every environment variable Blaster reads. The name is the contract: the API, the Convex backend, and the docs all read this manifest rather than hardcoding their own lists. A variable is status "active" when code reads it, or "planned" when the capability is declared but not wired yet, which requires a reason.

vars.name: TWENTY_BASE_URL
vars.description: Origin of the Twenty workspace, without a trailing slash. Records are read from ${TWENTY_BASE_URL}/rest/<object> and metadata from ${TWENTY_BASE_URL}/graphql.

vars.name: TWENTY_API_KEY
vars.description: Twenty API key, sent as a bearer token on every REST and GraphQL call. Never leaves the server.

vars.name: TWENTY_USER_EMAIL
vars.reason: Only needed by the direct-Postgres login path, which is not built. Blaster authenticates to Twenty with an API key today, so there is no user to attribute a login to yet.
vars.description: Workspace user email recorded alongside records Blaster writes, for audit.

vars.name: TWENTY_USER_PASSWORD
vars.reason: Belongs to the direct-Postgres login path, which is not built. Accepting a password would add a credential Blaster has no use for until that path exists.
vars.description: Workspace user password for the direct-Postgres login path. Prefer TWENTY_API_KEY.

vars.name: TWENTY_DATABASE_URL
vars.reason: Belongs to the direct-Postgres login path, which is not built. Opening a Postgres connection before anything queries it would be a credential with no reader.
vars.description: Read-only Postgres connection used solely to verify a workspace login against core."user". Requires SELECT on that table and nothing else.

vars.name: CONVEX_URL
vars.description: URL of the Convex deployment the API writes to. Required for the Telnyx webhook to store inbound messages; without it the webhook reports not-configured rather than pretending the message was saved. Every other route reads Twenty or Telnyx directly and does not need it.

vars.name: TELNYX_API_KEY
vars.description: Telnyx API key. Sending and profile listing both fail without it.

vars.name: TELNYX_MESSAGING_PROFILE_ID
vars.description: Catch-all profile for a number nobody has recorded one for. A workspace with several numbers cannot be described by one variable, so this is the fallback rather than the answer: the sending number's own agencyPhones.messagingProfileId decides its profile, and this is only consulted when that record has none. Set it only for a number you do not manage in Twenty.

vars.name: TELNYX_MESSAGING_PROFILE_US
vars.description: Profile whitelisted to US, backed by a 10DLC brand and campaign. Selected when the recipient resolves to the United States.

vars.name: TELNYX_MESSAGING_PROFILE_IE
vars.description: Profile whitelisted to IE and GB, carrying an alphanumeric sender. Selected when the recipient resolves to Ireland or the United Kingdom.

vars.name: TELNYX_MESSAGING_PROFILES
vars.description: The general country-to-profile mapping, in the compact form US=<id>,IE=<id>,GB=<id>. Any number of countries can be registered this way, and adding one is a configuration change rather than a code change. Takes precedence over the per-country variables.

vars.name: TELNYX_PUBLIC_KEY
vars.description: Telnyx public key used to verify inbound webhook signatures. Without it the receiver falls back to a shared-secret gate, which the response states.

vars.name: TELNYX_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
vars.description: Shared secret for the webhook receiver, used when no public key is configured to verify signatures.

vars.name: PORT
vars.description: Port the Hono server binds. Defaults to 4180.

vars.name: CI
vars.description: Set to true in automation. The CLI never opens interactive prompts when it is set, so scripted runs cannot hang waiting for input.

vars.name: TWENTY_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
vars.description: OAuth client id registered against the Twenty instance (RFC 7591). Required on the API host for the operator sign-in flow; the CLI and web app never hold it directly.

vars.name: TWENTY_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
vars.description: OAuth client secret for the confidential API-side client. Never leaves the server; the browser and CLI redeem through the API proxy instead.

vars.name: TWENTY_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI
vars.description: Exact redirect URI registered with Twenty, pointing at the web app /callback route. Must match on authorize and redeem calls.

vars.name: TWENTY_OAUTH_SCOPE
vars.description: Space-separated OAuth scopes requested from Twenty. Defaults to 'api profile'.

vars.name: TWENTY_BASIC_USER
vars.description: User half of the basic-auth gate in front of the Twenty instance. Required only when an auth-guard proxy fronts the deployment, and only together with TWENTY_BASIC_PASSWORD. The operator's browser gets a native prompt for it on /authorize; the API presents the same header for discovery, token, and introspection calls. The Bearer token alone is enough for /rest and /graphql, which a guard normally exempts.

vars.name: TWENTY_BASIC_PASSWORD
vars.description: Password half of the auth-guard gate. Unset means no gate is declared, not a guard that rejects everything, so the two variables must be set together. Never leaves the server.

vars.name: BLASTER_API_URL
vars.description: Origin of the Blaster Hono API. The CLI validates and refreshes Twenty operator tokens through it. Defaults to http://localhost:4180.

vars.name: BLASTER_WEB_URL
vars.description: Origin of the Blaster web app. `blaster login` opens its /login page there. Defaults to http://localhost:5173.
